A: Obstetric ultrasound image from a fetus with Patau syndrome demonstrating the golf ball sign (calcification of the mitral valve chordae), a recognized cardiac manifestation of the condition. B: Obstetric ultrasound image from a fetus with Patau syndrome showing left ventricular hypoplasia, consistent with hypoplastic left heart syndrome. C: Obstetric ultrasound image from a fetus with Patau syndrome demonstrating asymmetry of cardiac chambers with increased dimensions of the right heart chambers.

in_text_mentions: hypoplasia, low implantation of the ears, bilateral incisive transforaminal cleft lip and palate 7 (Figure 2A), hypotelorism with increased lens density (Figure 2B), bilateral polydactyly (Figure 3) of hands and feet, presence of golf-ball sign (calcification of the mitral valve chordae) (Figure 4A), and hypoplasia of left heart chambers, especially ventricular (Figure 4B). Regarding the other systems, it was confirmed: no closure defects in the vertebral column; intact abdominal wall, topical and normal-appearing stomach; usual-appearing liver and intestinal loops with standard echogenicity.

In addition, it was demonstrated low weight (6th percentile) and decreased head circumference (3rd percentile) for gestational age, severe facial malformations and heart disease, with increased dimensions of the right heart chambers (Figure 4C), myocardial hypertrophy and mild pericardial effusion, in addition to hepatic vein ectasia, suggestive of systemic congestion.

in_text_mentions: including the TORCH test (toxoplasma, rubella, cytomegalovirus, and herpes simplex virus), was negative. Hepatitis B surface antigen and antibody were non-reactive and the core antibody was negative. The blood culture did not show bacterial growth. On the 9th day of life, chromosomal analysis showed a female karyotype with three copies of chromosome number 13 (trisomy 13) in all 20 metaphase cell counts. Radiology investigations included head magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and revealed absence of scalp and calvarium at the parietal region with no herniation visualized, as shown in Figure 2.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of an infant with Patau syndrome showing visible cleft lip, with caption and in-text confirming additional classic Patau syndrome phenotypic features. B: Clinical photograph of the same infant with Patau syndrome showing cleft lip and ocular hypertelorism, consistent with described Patau syndrome phenotypic features.
panels.attribution_text: Aleksander et al. Beyond the Diagnosis: A Journey of an 8-Year-Old Girl with Patau Syndrome: Case Report.. Children (Basel, Switzerland) 2025. doi:10.3390/children12121632. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: The female patient with Patau syndrome as an infant presenting phenotypic changes in Trisomy 13, including cleft lip, trigger thumbs and rocker bottom feet.
in_text_mentions: ion, the patient exhibited several phenotypic features consistent with Patau syndrome, including cleft lip and palate, ocular hypertelorism, low-set ears, low anterior hairline, cutis aplasia, microcephaly, overlapping fingers, and rocker-bottom feet (Figure 1). No pulmonary, genital, renal abnormalities, or polydactyly were identified. Congenital heart defects, including ventricular septal defect (VSD), atrial septal defect (ASD), patent foramen ovale (PFO), and bicuspid aortic valve were identified; however, the girl remained hemodynamically stable and did not require cardiovascular support.

plate_findings.evidence: Caption: 'Presence of a single ventricle and fusion of the thalamus'; in-text: 'semilobar HPE with thalamic fusion and single first ventricle'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Obstetric ultrasound of a human fetus with Patau syndrome demonstrating classic semilobar holoprosencephaly with single ventricle and thalamic fusion, a well-documented neurological manifestation of the disease. B: Obstetric ultrasound of a human fetus with Patau syndrome demonstrating cerebellar vermis agenesis, a recognized central nervous system anomaly associated with the disease.
panels.attribution_text: Schlosser et al. Holoprosencephaly in Patau Syndrome.. Revista paulista de pediatria : orgao oficial da Sociedade de Pediatria de Sao Paulo 2023. doi:10.1590/1984-0462/2023/41/2022027. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Obstetric ultrasound showing neurological alterations in Patau syndrome: (1A). Presence of a single ventricle and fusion of the thalamus; (1B). Cerebellar vermis agenesis.
in_text_mentions: revious pregnancies. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of the patient's right hand showing postaxial polydactyly, explicitly attributed to trisomy 13/Patau syndrome by the caption and article context. B: Clinical photograph of the patient's left hand showing postaxial polydactyly, explicitly attributed to trisomy 13/Patau syndrome by the caption and article context. C: Clinical photograph of both feet showing postaxial polydactyly, explicitly attributed to trisomy 13/Patau syndrome by the caption and article context.

panels.figure_caption: Postaxial polydactyly is observed in both the right (A) and left (B) hands and also in the feet (C).
in_text_mentions: The hands presented six-finger symmetric postaxial polydactyly (Figure 2). The anus was imperforate. No macroscopic malformations of the nervous system were observed.

findings.label: Polycystic kidneys
findings.evidence: heterogeneous, dysplastic-appearing kidneys bilaterally with numerous scattered cysts in the renal parenchyma

panels.rationale: Coronal T2-weighted MRI demonstrating bilateral polycystic kidneys consistent with cystic renal dysplasia, a known classic manifestation of Patau syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Rennick et al. Congenital Hepatic Cyst in Patients With Patau Syndrome: A Rare Clinical Finding.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.46377. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Coronal T2-weighted image of the abdomen. The image demonstrates heterogeneous, dysplastic-appearing kidneys bilaterally with numerous scattered cysts in the renal parenchyma.
in_text_mentions: Incidentally, heterogeneous kidneys with diffuse tiny parenchymal cysts were observed on MRI, correlating with cystic renal dysplasia commonly described in Patau syndrome (Figure 4).
panels.copyright: Rennick et al. Congenital Hepatic Cyst in Patients With Patau Syndrome: A Rare Clinical Finding.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.46377. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
